findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed containers of pulled pork, baked beans and pasta to not be date marked. Items were marked with previous days date during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C
Observed coffee pots and baskets to be drying on cloth towels. Facility states that the towels are cleaned after every use. Discussed drying on clean sanitized counter top and using towels around the edge of counter to absorb any water that may run off. Dish draining pieces of equipment can also be used.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text: 3-201.11  (P) Food is not from an approved source. Comply with the food law regarding approved sources. Reference 3-201.11. Observed cheese sauce that appears to have been heated and cooled to the in the reach in cooler at the student ministries cafe. Cooling and reheating is considered a high risk process. The facility is licensed as a medium risk and shall either discard the cheese sauce and discontinue this practice or apply for a high risk permit. At this time the facility wants to remain a medium risk and has disposed of the cheese sauce and will discontinue the practice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The can opener in the ktichen fror #10 cans is soiled with dry soil. Take care to completely clan the can opener after each use. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have becone contaminated.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Platter used for storage of ice scoop on top of the ice machine was soiled with buildup of dust/general debris. Clean the storage platter as needed, and maintain it clean.

Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handles extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
740.830g - Bleach and Ultimate Sanitizer are available for use, but a chemical test kit was only available for checking bleach solutions. A quat test kit is also required for checking solutions made with Ultimate Sanitizer. Obtain a quat test kit. 

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) detachable pieces inside cappuccino machine (buildup);   and
B) inside ice machine -  bottom edge of black baffle (mold).

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.citation_text:
750.1030 - Hot water was not available at any of the faucets in the kitchen. Water heater was checked and reset a couple times. Employee that reset the water heater stated it kept kicking off and locking itself (digital readout read LOCKED). A call for service was made. (see general comments)

Water under pressure at the required temperature shall be provided to all fixtures and equipment that use water.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
750.800 - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) counter under coffee maker next to cappuccino machine (coffee splash/debris);
B) general surfaces inside the cappuccino machine (cappuccino mixes);   and
C) bottom inside the ovens (carbon/debris).

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors under coolers, freezer, ovens, and dry storage shelves were observed to have a general accumulation of dust and some debris. 

Clean the floors under equipment daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) Single service articles in pantry were observed uncovered (bowls and to go boxes). Store single service articles covered or inverted on a clean surface to protect items from potential contamination.
B) Toothpicks were observed with pick end rather than blunt ends extended up out of the holder. Store toothpicks with pick ends down inside the holder so only surfaces that will not go into food or a persons mouth will be touched when retrieving toothpicks.
Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.
